To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel nacre protein Nautilin‐‐63 is a glycoprotein that is highly glycosilated, acidic, able to bind chitine and to interact with CaCO3 crystals, but that it exhibits an extremely low ability to inhibit in vitro the precipitation of Ca‐CO3.
Nautilin 63 is a novel nacre matrix protein that is highly acidic and glycosylated.
Nautilin-63 is a novel acidic glycosylated protein, that it contains collagenous domains, and that it interacts with the nacreous layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical and structural characterization of Nautilin, a novel acidic nacre glycoprotein from Nautilus macrophalus.
the molecular characterization of Nautilin-63, an acidic glycoprotein that is a major nacre protein in the cephalopods.
the biochemical properties of Nautilin63, a new nacre matrix protein from the cephalopods Nautilus macrophalus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nautilin-63 is an acidic glycoprotein with chitin‐binding ability and collagenous‐like sequences, which is involved in the formation of nacreous microstructures in Nautilus macrophalus.

Nautilin is a new type of protein with a unique combination of structural features, and that its biological role in the formation and/or the stabilization of the nacreous layer remains to be determined.
the nacre matrix of Nautilus is more complex than previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nacre matrix of Nautilus macrophalus, like that of other molluscs, contains a large variety of soluble and insoluble macromolecules, each of which has its own specific biochemical and structural properties.
Nautilin63 exhibits a ‘hybrid’ protein nature, which is probably a consequence of its specific function in the nacreous layer of the Nautilus shell.
Nautilin is a new nacre protein that is likely involved in the regulation of the nacre microstructures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Nautilin63 is an acidic glycoprotein that may interact with the CaCO3 crystals and with the insoluble matrix components.

the nacre matrix proteins from the cephalopods Nautilus and Sepia are more similar to each other than previously thought, and that the nacreous layer of the cephalo‐ and gastropod shells are not as different as generally believed.
Nautilin is not an inhibitor of calcification but rather an organizer of nacre microstructure.
